purpose: Explain a contained synthetic service incident to a decision maker, including impact, response, uncertainty, and next action.

facts.text: At 09:10 UTC on 2026-03-04, the synthetic Cedar Queue status monitor first detected elevated delivery delay.
The delay affected 18 of 240 test messages submitted between 09:05 and 09:24 UTC.
All 18 affected test messages were eventually delivered by 09:41 UTC; none was lost.
The maximum observed delivery delay was 27 minutes, compared with the five-minute test objective.
A worker configuration change at 09:02 UTC reduced the synthetic queue polling concurrency from eight to two.
The team restored polling concurrency to eight at 09:26 UTC; delivery delay returned below five minutes by 09:33 UTC.
The configuration change and delay are temporally associated, but the available record does not prove sole causation.
No production traffic or customer accounts were involved in this synthetic exercise.
The synthetic on-call operator checked queue depth every five minutes until 10:00 UTC.
Proposed: A proposed follow-up is to add a predeployment check that refuses polling concurrency below four.
The root cause remains unconfirmed pending a replay that varies concurrency while holding input volume fixed.
The incident status was closed for response at 10:00 UTC, while cause investigation remained open.

sections.title: Incident and impact
sections.instruction: Summarize timeline, scale, delay, and synthetic scope.

sections.title: Response and status
sections.instruction: Describe configuration observation, response, restoration, and remaining causal uncertainty.

sections.title: Next action
sections.instruction: Describe the proposed guard and the confirming replay without claiming completion.

required_goals.acceptance: No material claim exceeds the supplied facts, including headings, lists, tables, and captions.
required_goals.method: Independent reviewer audits all factual text and planted negative assertions.

required_goals.method: Independent reviewer classifies material assertions against source status and explicit unknowns.
